Subject: Request: extended log TTL and deletion evidence for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Alex,

We're working through the latest SIG/CAIQ responses and have a Cardinal-specific requirement from our QA/regulatory team relating to audit/log retention. Our baseline SOC 2 requirement is to retain request and transaction logs for investigatory purposes for up to 180 days for certain regulated workloads.

Specifically:
- Can Redwood support a per-tenant log retention policy of 180 days for request-level logs (request metadata, timestamps, request IDs)?
- If so, what evidence can you provide to show that logs older than the tenant TTL are actually deleted (audit trail of deletions, job run timestamps, checksums, etc.)?
- We need a one-page statement or form we can include in our audit binder that confirms the deletion workflow and controls (who can change TTL, how deletion jobs are authenticated, and where audit logs are stored).

Attached is the SIG spreadsheet with Cardinal's markings (cardinal-sig-questions.xlsx). If this is an exception from your default, please outline the approval steps and expected turnaround.

Thanks,
Susan Evans
Director, IT Compliance
Cardinal Pharmaceuticals

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Request: extended log TTL and deletion evidence for SIG/CAIQ

Alex / team — brief technical confirmation and what we can deliver: we can support per-tenant request-log retention up to 365 days via a Customer Retention Exception (CRE). Our standard default retention for request metadata is 30 days. Exception workflow and controls (high level):

- Storage and immutability: Logs are written to an append-only write path and replicated to a WORM-backed S3 bucket with object lock enabled for the configured retention period. For exceptions we can route tenant log objects to a longer-lived prefix and set lifecycle rules accordingly.
- Deletion workflow: A scheduled, authenticated deletion job (retention-worker) reconciles current TTL settings and removes objects past retention. The worker runs in a restricted compute pool, signs actions with a KMS-backed service key, and writes a deletion transaction record to our immutable audit ledger (separate dataset).
- Audit evidence: We can export deletion transaction records (timestamp, object key prefix, deletion-job-id, initiating service principal) and a digest of pre- and post-deletion object counts. We will redact any payload-level PII — these are metadata-only records.
- Controls and approvals: CRE requests require Security + Ops sign-off; changes to TTL are tracked in change history and guarded by role-based access controls.

Deliverables we can provide to Cardinal within 7 business days after CRE approval:
1) Filled retention-exception-form (signed by Security lead) — this is the 1-page statement you requested.
2) Redacted deletion-audit-snippet.csv containing a sample of the deletion transaction records for the tenant (first/last 10 rows).
3) A zip of SIG-evidence artifacts pointing to our SOC 2 mapping (redwood-soc2-sig-mapping.pdf) — those are generic but we'll mark the fields relevant to Cardinal.

A couple notes: the deletion audit export is a metadata export (object keys, timestamps, job ids). We will not include raw request payloads. If Cardinal needs longer retention than 365 days, that requires legal review and infrastructure planning and is not on the standard CRE path.

Next steps: Alex — if Cardinal agrees to proceed, Grace can issue the CRE template to Cardinal for signature. Once signed, I'll schedule the export and produce the artifacts and a short controls statement.

-Hannah
